planting.note: Set out in spring in full sun to light shade on sandy, acidic, well-drained ground; the pink new growth shows best with consistent moisture through the first growing season.

directions: Woodlanders Nursery selected this form of Darrow's evergreen blueberry from sandy pinelands running from Georgia into Florida, choosing a Highlands County clone with new leaves that flush distinctly pink before settling into shiny blue-green. White to pale-pink spring flowers draw in bees ahead of a modest crop of small, sweet dark blue berries that birds find first. Like the species, it thrives in lean, acidic, fast-draining sand and resents soggy roots, making it well suited to the same low-input sites as native wiregrass flatwoods plantings. Use it as a flowering, color-changing low shrub in native or pollinator borders across the Gulf Coast's milder zones.
